steps.name: Sample structure QC
caveats: The import state of the Salmon table is unknown; do not re-normalize or transform the counts for modeling purposes in this step — only inspect and report the value types.
With pooled larvae there is no individual-level pairing; do not look for pairing structure.
steps.context: Inputs: /eval-four-models-v2-with-zebrafish-two-group-n3-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12000 genes x 6 samples, Salmon, Ensembl Danio rerio annotation; the record does not state whether length correction occurred) and /eval-four-models-v2-with-zebrafish-two-group-n3-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (6 rows, one per sample, condition column: treated vs control). Pooled larvae, unpaired, single batch. Organism: Danio rerio.
steps.question: Do the 3 treated and 3 control zebrafish larvae pools (6 samples, single batch) separate cleanly by condition in PCA, with no outlier or mislabeled sample, before any test is run?

grounding.reason: Sample structure QC: vst(blind), PCA, sample distances, library sizes per R-0033@40bf

steps.description: Per-sample library sizes, blind variance-stabilizing transformation, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, Euclidean sample-distance heatmap, all colored by condition; plus a check of the nature of the delivered count values (integer vs fractional), which determines how the lost-length-offset caveat is stated.
acceptance_criteria: PCA plot and sample-distance heatmap produced and colored by condition (3 treated vs 3 control)
Samples cluster by condition as the metadata states; any sample departing from its group or any sign of an identity swap is flagged and reported
Per-sample library sizes (median counts / total counts) reported; any sample far below the rest is flagged
The nature of the count values is determined and recorded: integer counts or fractional (scaled) values, which T1S2/T1S3 must state in the report

steps.name: DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm log fold change shrinkage
caveats: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

With two or three replicates per group, the design step states the expected power of the test before the model. The tools of record for a power and sample size calculation, RNASeqPower and PROPER, are not in the pool here. Compute the power from the closed form of the sample size in terms of the depth, the biological coefficient of variation, the fold change, and the significance level, or take the dispersion from a pilot or a public dataset of the same tissue, and state the fold change that the design can find with 80 percent power. State that a larger replicate count raises the power more than a deeper sequencing does. The statement is a caution on the plan and not a reason to loosen the threshold.

If the smallest group holds three replicates, the test has low power. Both count models find only a small share of the true differentially expressed genes, most of them with a large fold change. Interpret the result with caution, and state the power limit in the report. Keep alpha at its default value, and do not change the threshold to compensate for the small design. A gene that is not in the list is not shown to be unchanged.
steps.context: Inputs: counts.csv (12000 x 6, Ensembl Danio rerio IDs) and metadata.csv (condition: treated/control, 3+3). Fit the count model on the counts as delivered with NO length offset — the length-correction state of the Salmon table is not established and no per-sample quantification files or average transcript length table exist; state in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, and do not invent a length input. If T1S1 recorded fractional (scaled) values, DESeq2 will warn that counts are not integers; proceed and state this. With 3 replicates per group the design states expected power before the model: RNASeqPower and PROPER are not available in the pool, so compute power from the closed form in depth, biological CV, fold change, and significance level (or a public same-tissue dispersion), and state the fold change the design finds at 80% power.
steps.question: Which of the ~12000 Danio rerio genes differ in expression between the 3 treated and 3 control zebrafish larvae pools (adjusted p < 0.05)?

grounding.reason: DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm log fold change shrinkage per R-0029@22ca

steps.description: Minimal pre-filter, DESeq2 fixed-effects design ~ condition with explicit reference level control and contrast treated (numerator) vs control (denominator), median-of-ratios size factors inside the model, Wald test, apeglm shrinkage of the single coefficient, BH adjustment with independent filtering at alpha 0.05, Cook's-distance outlier flagging kept on, plus the MA plot, dispersion plot, and p-value histogram.
acceptance_criteria: Results table with baseMean, unshrunken log2FoldChange, shrunken log2FoldChange (apeglm), lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj, and a column separating filter-NA from outlier-NA genes
Number of genes tested after the pre-filter and number of DE genes at padj < 0.05 reported
Number of genes with NA padj from independent filtering reported separately from genes with NA pvalue from Cook's-distance outlier flagging (n < 7 per cell)
MA plot, dispersion plot, and unadjusted p-value histogram produced; histogram shape assessed before trusting adjusted p-values
Expected-power statement at 3 replicates per group computed (closed form) and stored for the report

steps.name: edgeR quasi-likelihood robustness check
caveats: edgeR on this design has no independent filtering; the filterByExpr-equivalent minimal pre-filter is what is shared with T1S2 so the compared universes differ only by method.
Low replicate count (3/group) inflates the method disagreement at low counts; report it, do not hide it.
steps.context: Inputs: same counts.csv and metadata.csv as T1S2. Apply the same pre-filter (keep a gene with at least 10 counts in at least the smallest group size of samples, i.e. 3). TMM scaling factors. Reference level control, contrast treated vs control. alpha 0.05, BH. Do not loosen any threshold to compensate for the small design.
steps.question: Does the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same 6-sample design call the same differentially expressed genes as the DESeq2 Wald test, and what is the overlap?

grounding.reason: Permitted alternative M-0003 (edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test) per rule R-0001@9a17, which names it the second method of the DESeq2 Wald test; chosen because the replicate count (3 per group) is at the low end where the alternative's 'when' clause says to run both and report the overlap of the two gene sets.

constraints: filter: same minimal pre-filter as T1S2 (>=10 counts in >=3 samples)
normalize: TMM scaling factors inside the quasi-likelihood model (doi:10.1186/s13059-014-0550-8 companion, R-0026@9ab1)
Report the intersection and both method-specific sets; do not present the union as the result (R-0042@54e1)
steps.description: Second method of record for robustness at the low-replicate end: identical minimal pre-filter, TMM normalization, fixed-effects design ~ condition with reference control, glmQLFit/glmQLFTest, BH at alpha 0.05; overlap of the two DE gene sets reported (intersection = high-confidence set, method-specific genes listed secondarily).
acceptance_criteria: edgeR QL DE table at padj < 0.05 (logFC, p, padj)
Overlap with the T1S2 DESeq2 set quantified: |intersection|, DESeq2-only, edgeR-only, and the intersection named as the high-confidence set
Same reference level (control) and contrast direction as T1S2, so fold-change signs are comparable

plan.title: Zebrafish larvae treated vs control DE + GO enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: Six whole-larva pools (3 treated, 3 control, unpaired, single batch) with 12000 gene-level Salmon counts on Ensembl Danio rerio IDs. The length-correction state of the delivered count table is not established (no per-sample quantification files or average transcript length table provided), so the counts are modeled as delivered with no length offset and that loss is reported, per R-0169. Flow: T1S1 verifies sample structure (blind vst, PCA on top 500 variable genes, sample distances) before any test; T1S2 runs the DESeq2 Wald test (minimal pre-filter of 10 counts in >=3 samples, median-of-ratios size factors inside the model, explicit reference level control, contrast treated vs control, apeglm LFC shrinkage, BH at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering, Cook's-distance outlier flagging kept on); T1S4 re-runs the identical design under edgeR quasi-likelihood as the robustness second method because 3 replicates per group is at the low end where the rule says to run both and report the overlap; T2S1 runs fgsea preranked GSEA on the full ranked list (Wald statistic, the side chosen for the R-0108 dispute) against Danio rerio GO sets from org.Dr.eg.db, because no zebrafish curated gene-set collection is provisioned in the environment (MSigDB Hallmark/GO is human and mouse only, WikiPathways is human/mouse/rat) and no offline orthology-mapping resource exists, so per R-0050 the organism's own GO is the species-matched path; T1S3 assembles the report with fit diagnostics, the power statement for 3 replicates, the edgeR overlap as the high-confidence set, and the enrichment provenance and limits.

steps.method: DESeq2 sample structure QC (vst blind, PCA, sample distances)
DESeq2 pre-filter minimal_then_independent
median-of-ratios size factors inside the model
DESeq2 fixed-effects design ~ condition
DESeq2 Wald test
apeglm log fold change shrinkage
BH adjustment with independent filtering at alpha 0.05
edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test
fgsea preranked on the full ranked list
report assembly with fit diagnostics and reproducibility record
Low count filter: keep a gene with at least 10 counts in at least the smallest group size of samples

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

With two or three replicates per group, the design step states the expected power of the test before the model. The tools of record for a power and sample size calculation, RNASeqPower and PROPER, are not in the pool here. Compute the power from the closed form of the sample size in terms of the depth, the biological coefficient of variation, the fold change, and the significance level, or take the dispersion from a pilot or a public dataset of the same tissue, and state the fold change that the design can find with 80 percent power. State that a larger replicate count raises the power more than a deeper sequencing does. The statement is a caution on the plan and not a reason to loosen the threshold.

If the smallest group holds three replicates, the test has low power. Both count models find only a small share of the true differentially expressed genes, most of them with a large fold change. Interpret the result with caution, and state the power limit in the report. Keep alpha at its default value, and do not change the threshold to compensate for the small design. A gene that is not in the list is not shown to be unchanged.

For an organism other than human or mouse, the knowledge plane serves no curated gene set collection. Map the genes to their human orthologs and use a human collection, or use the Gene Ontology annotation of the organism. Each path has a limit. An ortholog map drops each gene without a one-to-one human ortholog, and the GO annotation of a less studied organism is thin. State the path and its limit in the report.

If fewer than about 50 genes pass the significance threshold, do not run an over-representation test on that list. A hypergeometric test of a short list finds no category, and a change of the threshold changes the list and the result. Run the ranked method on the full list of tested genes instead, because it finds a set of genes with a small but coordinated change that no single gene shows. State the size of the significant list in the report.
